subject: general
question: _________ of the Constitution of India has provisions for legal enforcement of the fundamental rights.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 32**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 32** of the Constitution of India provides for the legal enforcement of the fundamental rights.
 
• It grants the right to individuals to approach the Supreme Court for the enforcement of these rights.
 
• This article is often referred to as the "heart and soul" of the Constitution by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, one of the principal architects of the Constitution.
 
• Under Article 32, the Supreme Court has the power to issue writs, including habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto, and certiorari, for the enforcement of fundamental rights.
 
• It ensures that the fundamental rights of individuals are protected and can be enforced through the judiciary.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental rights** are enshrined in Part III of the Constitution of India.
 
• These rights are considered essential for the overall development of individuals and are guaranteed against state actions.
 
• Article 32 is a crucial aspect of the Constitution as it provides a direct remedy for the violation of fundamental rights.
 
• Dr. B.R. Ambedkar emphasized the importance of Article 32, stating that without it, the Constitution would be a nullity.
 
• The Supreme Court of India, through its power under Article 32, acts as the protector and guarantor of fundamental rights.
